model.description: Fixed-denominator fidelity loss for the T3 Code Web to Lynx-for-Web to Lynxtron Native port.

points.label: First archived matched geometry
points.narrative: New Thread exposed a 216px focal geometry miss and complete content drift; Settings and the populated Sidebar were already structurally close.

points.label: Exact-owned Native readiness
points.narrative: Three isolated starts proved the main-owned transport, advancing sequence, canonical thread/model identity, and zero renderer errors.

points.label: Seven-state Browser matrix
points.narrative: The first dual-renderer matrix proved identity and readiness across 14 cells. It also exposed that green harness geometry baselines were not visual parity.

points.label: 39-state strict evidence matrix
points.narrative: Plan 11C expanded the denominator to 39 product states. Browser content coverage became broad, while Native evidence remained intentionally sparse and R5/R10 blockers stayed explicit.

points.label: First Native pixel baseline
points.narrative: A real Web/Native comparison measured 4.467 MAE and 5.86% significant-pixel share across the full 1280×820 frame.

points.label: Masked pixel residual convergence
points.narrative: After deterministic timer masking, full-frame residual fell to 1.1009 MAE and 1.2763% significant pixels; Composer, Sidebar, Header, and Transcript regions became independently measurable.

points.label: Four-state review interaction matrix
points.narrative: Four combinations of Sidebar and changed-files state passed exact-owned Native interaction and geometry checks; card-region SSIM improved from 0.7492 to 0.8758.

points.label: Model Picker fidelity closeout
points.narrative: Browser geometry reached zero panel delta; Native proved main transport, exact 360×346 panel geometry, real-tap dismissal, scrolling, search, favorites, and provider/model selection. Selected-state pixels remained explicitly pending.

points.label: Evidence archaeology reset
points.narrative: The product did not regress. Archaeology removed stale pixels and demoted pre-final5 claims, so current-head evidence confidence falls while historical observed residual remains intact.

attribution.reason: This loss decrease comes from the first current-head Browser measurement after the archaeology reset, not from a measured product change between commits.

points.label: Current-head docked Composer browser pair
points.narrative: The isolated Web/Lynx pair matched six Composer geometry anchors, controls, context labels, semantic state, and clean readiness. Placeholder copy and material pixels remain visibly different; interaction and Native claims remain unmeasured.

attribution.reason: A before/after Browser pair measures one working-tree product change: Web and Lynx now consume the same session-phase placeholder projection.

points.label: Docked Composer placeholder parity
points.narrative: A shared session-phase placeholder projection removed the only measured Composer content mismatch. All nine content anchors now match, geometry remains exact, and Composer/context SSIM improves from 0.894106 to 0.914911. Native and interaction claims remain unmeasured.

attribution.reason: A before/after Native interaction investigation isolated and removed the Sidebar-only width transition while retaining the same scope, weights, and pointer sample sequence.

points.label: Native Sidebar resize cursor tracking
points.narrative: A new interaction scope records the Native Sidebar resize. The product previously applied every pointer sample through a 200ms width transition, visibly trailing the cursor. During drag the transition is now disabled, and ten retained geometry samples in each direction match cursor-derived width with 0px maximum error. Lynx-for-Web remains unmeasured for interaction and retains unknown loss.

attribution.reason: Classification only: historical runtime evidence cannot be promoted to a current-head product residual without matching final5 captures.

points.label: Review diff current-head evidence blocker
points.narrative: No product loss is recorded. The apparent review-diff residual of 1.0 comes from a historical R10 runtimeBlocked gate while the final5 manifest still marks Web, Lynx-for-Web, and Native review evidence pending. This is a capture/evidence mismatch and remains outside product-loss attribution until one canonical snapshot is captured on all required clients.

attribution.reason: Current-head canonical captures supersede stale runtime-blocker evidence without attributing the evidence correction to a product code change.

points.label: Current-head Hero and Sendable Composer pair
points.narrative: Canonical Web and Lynx-for-Web captures share one server, snapshot, new-thread route, dark theme, density, project, and 1280x820 viewport. Hero and Sendable content, geometry, controls, context labels, input, and primary action match. The old 62.64% residual was historical runtime-blocker evidence plus a placeholder extractor mismatch; current measurable product loss is material pixels.

attribution.reason: One CSS-only product change was measured against the same canonical Hero snapshot and viewport before and after.

points.label: Hero Composer footer material parity
points.narrative: Lynx removed its footer-only vertical offset and fixed control widths, then aligned horizontal padding and transparent border box sizing with Web. Footer SSIM improves from 0.746677 to 0.843791 and Composer-region SSIM improves from 0.901043 to 0.923045.

points.label: Lifecycle reconnecting parity
points.narrative: A corrected fault harness waits for Lynx branch discovery before terminating the owned server, separating early-fault noise from product loss. On the stable parent commit, content and semantic Composer pixels already match, but Lynx alone renders the lifecycle banner above the draft hero and shifts the Composer 31px downward. The product fix suppresses that separate hero banner and retains the last known model presentation while unavailable. The after capture passes every gate with 24 zero-delta geometry anchors and improves full-frame SSIM from 0.866145 to 0.914674. Native recovery and reconnect interaction remain unmeasured.

attribution.reason: A corrected empty-transcript readiness gate established the current-head product baseline without assigning the evidence correction to product code.

points.label: Current idle-thread Sidebar baseline
points.narrative: The corrected harness recognizes the seeded idle thread as an intentionally empty transcript after Web thread sync settles. The earlier non-empty transcript failure was capture timing noise and is not product loss. On the stable matched snapshot, Sidebar row geometry is a real product residual: Web rows are 239px wide at x=8 while Lynx rows are 255px wide at x=9 and shifted 3px downward. Empty-transcript copy remains different and is deliberately not overwritten by this checkpoint.

attribution.reason: The same Browser snapshot and viewport were captured before and after commit d9d2444e5, and a fresh exact-bundle Native geometry gate independently verified rail containment.

points.label: Idle-thread Sidebar row containment
points.narrative: Lynx now accounts for the shared Sidebar group's 16px horizontal padding, removes the stale one-by-three-pixel list calibration, and bounds row cards. Both Browser rows now match Web at x=8 with width 239px and identical y/height. The remaining 15px card-wrapper height difference and low Sidebar material SSIM stay visible. A fresh 1280x820 Native run loads the exact staged bundle, advances the main transport sequence, renders the canonical thread, and proves all three 225px rows and 78px cards remain inside the 256px rail; it is containment evidence, not a Native pixel residual.

attribution.reason: Hero and Sendable use the same snapshots and viewports on the direct parent and product commit, with a fresh exact-bundle Native icon geometry gate.

points.label: Composer Footer icon geometry
points.narrative: Direct parent-commit before/after captures show that Web uses 14px chevrons, a 16px runtime icon, and an 18px Build icon while Lynx used 12px, 14px, and 14px respectively. The committed fix aligns those semantic icon boxes and chevron optical margins. Hero Footer SSIM improves from 0.843611 to 0.845620 and Sendable Footer SSIM improves from 0.840541 to 0.842550. Composer-region residual improves by 0.000185 in each state. A fresh exact-bundle Native run independently proves three 14px chevrons, one 16px runtime icon, and one 18px Build icon with main transport sequence advancement and zero renderer errors; it is geometry/readiness evidence, not a Native pixel-residual update.

attribution.reason: Hero and Sendable use the same snapshots and viewports before and after the single-token product commit, with a fresh staged Native token gate.

points.label: Composer Footer label alpha
points.narrative: Web renders Composer Footer labels with the shared muted foreground at 70% alpha while Lynx previously used the same base color fully opaque. The one-token fix improves Hero Footer SSIM from 0.845620 to 0.853794 and Sendable Footer SSIM from 0.842550 to 0.850723. Composer-region residual improves by 0.001408 in both states. A fresh exact-bundle Native run resolves the 70% token to 178/255 alpha, within one 8-bit quantization step, with main transport advancement and zero renderer errors; Native pixel parity is not claimed.

attribution.reason: Hero and Sendable use matched current snapshots around the icon-only product change, with an exact-bundle Native Context icon gate.

points.label: Composer Context icon geometry
points.narrative: The branch control used external SVG wrappers that ignored their requested 12px dimensions and rendered as 24x18 leaves in Lynx-for-Web. Replacing them with the shared Icon primitive raises Hero Context SSIM from 0.898714 to 0.918270 and Sendable Context SSIM to 0.918089. Composer-region residual improves by about 0.004838 in each state. A fresh exact-bundle Native run proves three approximately 12px Context icons, main transport advancement, and zero renderer errors; Native pixel parity is not claimed.

attribution.reason: Hero and Sendable use matched current snapshots around the control-flow product change, with leaf-level Browser geometry and an exact-bundle read-only Native gate.

points.label: Composer Context control geometry
points.narrative: Matched control-leaf measurements showed that stale Lynx translations, padding, and missing Web border/SVG margin rules—not the strip bounds—caused the remaining Context control displacement. Replacing those optical offsets with the authority box model reduces checkout control width delta from 7.016px to 0.016px and branch width delta from 6.141px to 0.141px without fixed widths. Hero Context SSIM rises from 0.918270 to 0.942750 and Sendable Context SSIM rises from 0.918089 to 0.942568. A fresh exact-bundle Native run proves four 12px icons, two 24px controls, main transport advancement, and zero renderer errors; Native pixel parity is not claimed.

attribution.reason: Matched Hero and Sendable snapshots isolate the label-only product change; localized absolute-error accounting identifies its component contribution and the exact-bundle Native gate covers the changed typography.

points.label: Composer Context label typography
points.narrative: Localized pixel accounting showed that the checkout label alone contributed 68.8% of the remaining Context-strip absolute error, while the central background contributed only 6.7%. Removing stale synthetic stroke/scaling and half-pixel offsets, then matching Web's 70% muted color and 16px line height, reduces total Context absolute error by 41.8%. Hero Context SSIM rises from 0.942750 to 0.980469 and Sendable Context SSIM rises from 0.942568 to 0.980288. A fresh exact-bundle Native run proves both labels at 12px/500, 16px height and line height, 70% muted alpha, main transport advancement, and zero renderer errors; Native pixel parity is not claimed.

attribution.reason: Matched dark Hero and Sendable snapshots isolate the exact-raster product change; source-contract tests prevent stale path/fallback regression, and exact-bundle Native plus matched light diagnostic evidence cover both rendering targets.

points.label: Composer Context exact icon rasters
points.narrative: The branch icon still used stale Lucide path data and had no #818181 raster at any selectable size, causing Icon to fall back to an 18px white PNG and downscale it to 12px. Syncing GitBranch to Lucide 0.564, generating exact 12px dark/light Context variants, and preferring exact-size assets raises branch-icon SSIM from 0.684822 to 0.974066. Hero Context SSIM rises from 0.980469 to 0.983169 and Sendable Context SSIM rises from 0.980288 to 0.982988 without geometry changes. A fresh exact-bundle Native run verifies four 12px icons, preserved controls/labels, main transport advancement, and zero renderer errors. A matched light Hero diagnostic also passes and confirms muted rather than white fallback; its broader Context material remains a separately registered scope and does not overwrite whole-state light evidence.

attribution.reason: Matched light Browser evidence supplies the whole-Composer residual; dark byte identity rules out regression, while exact-theme Native DOM and pixel evidence prove the shared ramp rather than the rejected Browser-only gradient.

points.label: Composer light Context shared material
points.narrative: The newly validated light Hero scope matched snapshot, state, theme, and viewport, then localized 64% of Context absolute error to the top material ramp. Web authority showed a 221-to-254 glass-shadow profile while Lynx used five near-white bands. A CSS gradient improved Browser Preview but rendered flat on Native, so it was classified as a cross-surface product gap and superseded.
